audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Numbers / Bemidbar Balaam blessing-oracle text tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for seven-altars ritual, first and second oracles, inability to curse the blessed, Israel's distinctness, poetic innocence language, Exodus strength, anti-divination claim, and lion imagery.

verses.restored: Balaam said to Balak, Build for me here seven altars and prepare for me here seven bulls and seven rams.

familiar.text: And Balaam said unto Balak, Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven oxen and seven rams.

modern.text: Then Balaam said to Balak, “Build for me seven altars here, and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בִּלְעָם֙ אֶל בָּלָ֔ק בְּנֵה לִ֥י בָזֶ֖ה שִׁבְעָ֣ה מִזְבְּחֹ֑ת וְהָכֵ֥ן לִי֙ בָּזֶ֔ה שִׁבְעָ֥ה פָרִ֖ים וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה אֵילִֽים

verses.restored: Balak did as Balaam spoke, and Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

familiar.text: And Balak did as Balaam had spoken; and Balak and Balaam offered on every altar a bullock and a ram.

modern.text: So Balak did as Balaam had instructed, and Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ בָּלָ֔ק כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר בִּלְעָ֑ם וַיַּ֨עַל בָּלָ֧ק וּבִלְעָ֛ם פָּ֥ר וָאַ֖יִל בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ

verses.restored: Balaam said to Balak, Station yourself by your burnt offering, and I will go; perhaps YHWH will meet me. Whatever he shows me I will tell you. And he went to a bare height.

familiar.text: And Balaam said unto Balak, Stand by thy burnt offering, and I will go: peradventure the LORD will come to meet me: and whatsoever he sheweth me I will tell thee. And he went to an high place.

modern.text: “Stay here by your burnt offering while I am gone,” Balaam said to Balak. “Perhaps the LORD will meet with me. And whatever He reveals to me, I will tell you.” So Balaam went off to a barren height,

verses.restored: Divine met Balaam, and he said to him, I have arranged seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

familiar.text: And God met Balaam: and he said unto him, I have prepared seven altars, and I have offered upon every altar a bullock and a ram.

modern.text: and God met with him. “I have set up seven altars,” Balaam said, “and on each altar I have offered a bull and a ram.”

modern.text: How can I curse what God has not cursed? How can I denounce what the LORD has not denounced?

modern.text: For I see them from atop the rocky cliffs, and I watch them from the hills. Behold, a people dwelling apart, not reckoning themselves among the nations.

verses.restored: Who has counted dust of Jacob or numbered fourth part of Israel? Let my soul/life die death of upright, and let my end be like his.

familiar.text: Who can count the dust of Jacob, and the number of the fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his!

modern.text: Who can count the dust of Jacob or number even a fourth of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous; let my end be like theirs!”

modern.text: Then Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I brought you here to curse my enemies, and behold, you have only blessed them!”

familiar.text: And Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered a bullock and a ram on every altar.

modern.text: So Balak did as Balaam had instructed, and he offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ בָּלָ֔ק כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֣ר בִּלְעָ֑ם וַיַּ֛עַל פָּ֥ר וָאַ֖יִל בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ

translation_notes: Balaam's oracles transform a commissioned curse into blessing; royal payment and repeated ritual cannot purchase a different word.
'Dwelling apart' is poetic description of distinct identity in this oracle, not a timeless command for ethnic isolation, segregation, or supremacy.
Verse 21's claim that no iniquity is seen is covenant-poetic language in context, not a claim that Israel or its leaders are morally flawless.
The text rejects enchantment and divination as effective against the blessed people; it is not a manual for counter-magic.
Wild-ox and lion imagery expresses ancient strength and victory rhetoric and must not authorize modern violence or dehumanization.
Balak repeatedly changes Balaam's viewpoint in hopes of controlling the outcome, while the blessing remains resistant to manipulation.
safety_note: Do not use Numbers 23 to promote ethnic supremacy, segregation, magical warfare, antisemitic curse traditions, or nationalist violence. The core movement is the failure of paid power to turn a people into the object of a curse.
